notes.title: Update 1.2
notes.content:
Greetings, Project Apocalypse survivors!

I'm excited to introduce a major update that enhances various aspects of your gaming experience. Here's a concise summary of the key changes:

[h3]User Interface Overhaul:[/h3]
[list]
[*] Completely revamped UI for improved readability, visual appeal, and overall user experience.
[/list]

[h3]Visual and Gameplay Enhancements:[/h3]
[list]
[*] Added the Minimap and reworked the Fog of war system.
[*] Enhanced player camera control.
[*] Introduced new building models for houses and the radio tower.
[/list]

[h3]Gameplay Improvements:[/h3]
[list]
[*] Refined AI behavior for both survivors and infected.
[*] New Infected Type, the Hunter, a formidable new enemy that hunts survivors.
[*] Overall increased game difficulty and challenge for a more engaging experience.
[*] Tweaked game balance, including increased resources, resource drops from defeated infected, faster production, and item rebalancing.
[*] Improved morale system for survivors, resulting in fewer deaths and better gameplay flow.
[/list]

[h3]Bug Fixes:[/h3]
[list]
[*]Extensive bug fixes across various aspects of the game to enhance overall stability and performance. Fixed a lot of critical problems in AI, job management system and save game loading.
[/list]

I hope I managed to cover most of the issues and problems of Project Apocalypse, which you and I were able to find and report from the launch time. Thank you for your support, feedback, and valuable ideas. This update should make the game better in every aspect and now I can finally continue to work on initially planned Raids and Events, which will be available in one of the next updates.

Warm Regards,
The Project Apocalypse Development Team ;-)

notes.title: What's next for Project Apocalypse?
notes.content:
Hi there!

I wanted to give you a small update about the plans. The last six months were a bit intense work-wise and it heavily affected my original timeline for the updates. Nonetheless, I analyzed all your feedback (thank you!) and have been slowly implementing the new and promised features and fixing the most annoying problems. I'm not sure about the concrete date for the next update, but I want to at least tell you that it's in progress and the project itself is not abandoned at any point :)

You can always check the current Bugs, Plans, and Tasks spreadsheet: [url=https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1gKzBnCz_hlXPontfUKqBwC3ze1hvDPSSr9vegWvOmIQ/edit?usp=sharing]LINK[/url]

I switched to Unreal Engine 5.2 lately, though there aren't many benefits for a low-poly stylized game graphics-wise. But still, it's nice to be working with the up-to-date tools and it didn't cause any problems.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35874280/11da8536872fa605bce8c9ed2a96943aa6d37b32.png[/img]

There is a bunch of annoying bugs with weapon management, survivor's behavior, and overall UX. I've been experimenting with the direct control of the survivors, still not sure if it's the right thing to do, but maybe it can be combined with the current indirect control system.

I've also prepared a bunch of new events and some base systems for the raids - though there is one major problem with them. Currently, the whole system is based on characters living in the camp. And it's actually quite a task to add the ability to get some of your survivors out of the camp (even without the visualization) and keep them there during the raids, while still managing them and assuring the internal camp manager that everything is fine and there are some survivors left alive. Actually, while writing this I got an idea - if I change the Lose condition for the game and make it dependent only on the main base destruction and not the death of the last survivor - it should be fine. I'll try it.

So, as always, stay tuned. I try to push at least the small patch with the critical issues fixed soon.

notes.title: Project Apocalypse v1.0 released!
notes.content:
Attention all base-building fans! Project Apocalypse is finally here!

In this post-apocalyptic game, you'll have the opportunity to build and manage a camp of survivors, facing off against the dangers of a world overrun by the infected. With two game modes (Survival and Sandbox), 15 different buildings to choose from, and a fully-featured trade and production system, there's plenty to keep you busy as you work to build the ultimate camp.

After a successful Early Access period of 1.5 years, Project Apocalypse is now complete and ready for you to dive in. Whether you're a seasoned base-building pro or new to the genre, this game has something for everyone.

So what are you waiting for? Head over to the forum to suggest new features, and stay tuned for updates as we develop and improve the game. We can't wait for you to join us in the post-apocalyptic world of Project Apocalypse!

notes.title: Patch 0.9.9 - Pre-release!
notes.content:
Hi there! It has been a long journey - way longer than I expected - but Project Apocalypse is close to the release. The game is feature-complete in the current stage. However, some plans were cut and will be implemented as free updates later. Nothing too important, all the core is here and ready to play!

There also will be a few small patches between this one and the release version - I still need to address several problems with the Job system, enemy spawning, and weapon management. You will be okay with the current patch, but some minor inconsistencies can be a little annoying. I hope to fix them in the next few days and the final release patch will be available around December 20. 

[b]The changelog for this patch is not that big, but still, let's go through it:[/b]
[list]
[*] The Trade system is here! Build the shop and trade with other NPC-controlled camps. Finally some usage for late-game resources and items
[*] Bunch of new decorations to finally make your camp unique and aesthetically pleasing
[*] Added Currency as a resource. And also added the missing Fuel icon to the resources panel
[*] Overall readability and UX tweaks in most of the game interfaces
[*] No more bleeding buildings (yay!)
[*] Fixed ammo consumption
[*] Survivor's needs now loading correctly
[*] Survivors can now eat Rations
[*] Job creation and cancelation tweaks
[*] Incorrect building scaling after loading the game fix
[*] New icon for Junk
[*] Improved camera behavior and collision
[*] Needs balance tweaks (hunger and thirst mostly)
[*] Infinite water consumption fix (though it was an internal build problem, it's so cool!)
[/list]

I'm quite happy with the result and with the overall journey that we've had. I hope you'll enjoy this patch and the next one too :-)

Have a great weekend!

[b]p.s.[/b]
I'll use this post to congratulate the team of Dwarf Fortress on a successful steam release. It is one of the most inspiring games for me. It had a huge influence on Project Apocalypse and the overall itch "to make a base-building game with survivors!", even though I have like 0.1% of Dwarf Fortress gameplay depth. Still, I'm very happy that a lot of new players can try it now with simplified and more accessible controls and UI. Congratulations!

Try Dwarf Fortress, it's an amazing game: [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/975370/Dwarf_Fortress/]https://store.steampowered.com/app/975370/Dwarf_Fortress/[/url]

notes.title: Patch 0.9.0 is LIVE!
notes.content:
I can't believe it, but the new version of Project Apocalypse is finally here! It took almost a year to develop (not constantly, but still). And I'm a bit scared because of it. From one side, the game is now almost feature-complete and quite fun to play. On the other side - there can be a lot of problems and bugs because there are so many changes and so little testing (by me). Well, I'm going to monitor the active problems and fix them ASAP. Furthermore, now I can finally switch to more frequent and smaller patches. It was the original plan, but I failed. But now I can improve the whole patch pipeline.

So, what has changed? I wish to make CrusaderKings3-style patch notes with hundreds of elements, but let's start with the major features and changes.

New buildings. Each one (well, except for the radio station) has been remade from the ground. Three levels of upgrade for each building and five levels for the Main base. Upgrades unlock new features and items for production. 

New resources. They are grouped into four categories - Consumables, Materials, Goods, and Weapons. You need consumables to keep your survivors alive, Materials to build and craft, Goods to trade (coming in the next update), and Weapons to protect your camp. The production system has been remade and now you can add items to the production queue.

AI has been reworked from scratch. I switched the overall approach and now everything is working faster and can be extended much easier. There are some new behaviors like "retreat from the combat if scared", "find a campsite and rest there with fellow survivors", "go to the infirmary and heal there" and much more is going to be added in the next updates. 

There are two working game modes - Survival and Sandbox. In survival, you need to survive as long as possible. And in the sandbox, you can control different aspects and systems of the game to tweak your experience or just to build a pretty cool camp :-)

I'm going to reorganize the plans for the next updates and, finally, the release of the game. Stay tuned for news, write your ideas and feedback in the comments or discussions and enjoy the game! Thank you for playing and for being with me on this insane journey of evening-indie-game developer!

And here goes the CK3-Style patch note with SOME of the changes which I didn't forget to document:

[b]Project Apocalypse. Patch 0.9.0 Changelog:[/b]
- New buildings
- Reworked building construction price calculation
- Reworked building system, now you need to do some work on the construction site to build something
- Reworked job creation, use right click on objects to create a job
- Reworked production UI
- Reworked upgrade UI
- Reworked building efficiency system. Now it uses Fuel, Building Level, and the availability of the worker in the building
- Reworked Farm logic
- Healthbar fixes
- AI fixes
- Survivors leave the building if it is destroyed
- Inventory rework + removed inventory from most of the buildings
- Simplified resource management
- Reworked tutorial and How to Play panel
- Context naming for jobs
- Production queue logic
- Sleeping survivors can miss the infected attack
- Reworked needs balance
- New needs for survivors
- Building levels reworked. Leveling up unlocks new production schematics and increases the efficiency
- Massive performance optimization
- Resource points rebalanced
- Improved buildings and resource points collisions
- Infinite smaller fixes, tweaks, and improvements

[b]Known issues:[/b]
- The lounge, Garage, Shop, and Guard Tower are disabled in this build and will be activated later on. You can build them for decorative purposes
- AI can behave a bit strange. Please report anything that seems broken.

notes.title: Polishing the next update
notes.content:
Okay, I switched to notepad from my task tracker and even from the excel table. And it's perfect! Instant task creation and management.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35874280/0d9f996017739ff8627bca562a1cc6ec47c46a55.png[/img]

So, fixed a bunch of stuff during the last few days. Removed the production logic from the farm and made it just a building in which you can work inside. The new production system is highly dependent on the production queue and manages the work orders for survivors. And it just doesn't work for farms, which should grow food independently. 

27 tasks to go. A lot more will be added during the testing. But some of them are also already done, but I need to test them. Most of the tasks are related to building upgrades that are ready but never were properly tested.

Maybe I'll move shop and garage logic to another patch. Or I can try to implement them in some basic state, who knows 🙂

I'm also failing my internal deadline for the patch (August 1), but that's probably okay. I still have one free day to make a final push.

I like the current speed and the overall process of polishing and improving the existing features and mechanics. I missed that part of my job a lot. Stay tuned! 😉

notes.title: New building system!
notes.content:
Hi there!

Two years after the initial request, I implemented the new building system. The visual part is still WIP, though. But overall - now the building construction is not instantaneous but requires the actual survivor to come to the building site and do some work there. 

[previewyoutube=ylCbywEfJg0;full][/previewyoutube]

I skipped the whole resource logistics part, my earlier experiments with it were really boring. So, you need to bring gathered resources to the main base and that's all - they are becoming available for every building, construction, production, and survivor anywhere. Yay for sci-fi elements 😃

Though, I may return to this whole "bring resources from one building to another" system later on, if I'll finish everything else and will be really bored.

Will be available in the next update. And I hope I'll be able to push the development build in steam beta branch in a few days.

Stay tuned! ;-)

notes.title: New AI system, yay!
notes.content:
Good news, everyone!  I've switched from Unreal Engine's behavior tree to Logic Driver for dealing with AI. And it is incredible. I managed to move almost everything from the old system to the new one and now I can work with AI much faster. And it's way easier to implement new behavior for my survivors. I just wanted to share that news with you :-)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35874280/07849a912ba6fdf7cda4b09e73d747e8344614cf.png[/img]

Over the next few weeks, I'm going to implement most of the planned AI behavior and states. It's time to teach my survivors how to use the new buildings. what to do in their free time INSTEAD of constantly drinking at the bar and how to fight efficiently. They already can drink in multiple bars, heal in the infirmary (or with bandages if available), keep their distance from the infected (kind of), and do most of the jobs around the camp without problems and bugs (yay!)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35874280/0f221527c21fc894d36cadf2fc2a0ccc4aba4ef1.png[/img]

Finally, I resumed my work on the gameplay and mechanics, instead of working with 3d graphics and new buildings. I missed that part of my work and it's great to be back in action. I've redone the resources UI. Still not final, but looks way better and more straightforward than before. I've been constantly testing the game for the last two weeks and it was tough to understand which of the resources you need and what are they in general. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35874280/c33f44a162f698fc7977a389c64f99d62b2b5322.jpg[/img]

So, I hope some of you are still waiting for the update. And I hope it will be a good one and the game will be actually quite fun to play, with all the things I've planned for it. Stay tuned ;-)

notes.title: DevBlog - May 2022
notes.content:
Hi there! The last two months were, well, filled with unplanned and unpredicted activities and events. But I'm trying to get back to the development of Project Apocalypse. Yesterday, I've finished modeling the new buildings - it was almost a month-long task, but the main part is completed. They are not perfect and some still need to be improved (because my skill and pipeline improved during this month), but it's a huge step forward to the next game update. I want to share a few renders with you:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35874280/ea4d40b02bb455eb348f174d926ef72a90c2c986.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35874280/8aa8756cf507eda2fa235aaade6ab2d41c260615.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35874280/19aaa7ef7901dec4ed3129fe913b7b00e26284ab.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35874280/aece10745bb0363e190cedf6dc71b664cadf2086.png[/img]

Now, after another small iteration of polishing, all these buildings need to be implemented in-game. 18 buildings with three levels of upgrade (so, 56 models, yay!). Some of them are already presented in-game, but for most of the new ones, I still need to add more logic and gameplay. Still, it will be really nice to finally get back to Unreal Engine and do some programming (outside of my main work).

So, despite the delay, I'm happy with how things are moving on with the game. I wish it would be faster, but at the same time, I'm glad that my brain is returning to a normal and productive state (well, kind of). Thank you for your support and stay tuned ;-)

notes.title: DevBlog - January 2022
notes.content:
Hey guys! This is another project status update, yay!

Still working on a patch. Most of the planned stuff is implemented and now it's time to polish everything. For example, now you can see upgrade information for every building, but the UI is terrible and needs to be reworked.

I wish I had more time available, but for now, I can only do small work sessions here and there and this slows the development down a bit. I'll take note of it for my further projects, the overall scope should be much smaller. But hey, it's my first standalone project and errors should be made, right?

So, now it's polishing time. UI, gameplay balance, buildings, ai tweaks, and all that stuff. I won't give the ETA for the next update, but I'm working on it, don't worry, and thank you for your support and feedback!

notes.title: DevBlog - December 2021
notes.content:
Hi there! December is almost over, so it's time for another project status update. 

I'm refactoring the building and production system. Most of the tasks are done (you can always check the public task tracker with actual bugs and issues). Now you can build tier-based buildings, upgrade them up to three times and unlock new production schematics and buildings. 

The infected spawn system is also reworked to provide a better experience. Now infected are passive during the day and more aggressive after dusk. I hope with further tweaks, this will provide noticeable safe and danger cycles for your camps. 

With most of the hard tasks behind, I'm looking forward to releasing the next update in late January 2022. It's going to be the largest patch yet and will finally bring the game much closer to the original “build, manage, survive” vision.

notes.title: DevBlog - November 2021
notes.content:
Hi there! I would like to share with you what's currently is going on with Project Apocalypse.

I'm working on the next update and it's going to be a huge one. 20 buildings (with upgrades), reworked production, resources, and AI. I hope to fill the current lack of content with it and finally, most of the planned mechanics will be implemented. 

The list of available buildings is finalized until the release. Finally, there will be advanced buildings like Gunsmith or Trade Post and the overall camp building is going to be better. There are now different tiers of buildings with upgrades and dependencies. You'll start with the basic, primitive camp and will be able to expand and improve it.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35874280/f63d5991a7a1fc3897cf3be038398c58bd38375a.png[/img]

The resources in the game are also reworked completely. There is still a lot to improve in the field of UI and UX, but the overall resource list looks way better. You have basic resources like materials, cloth, metal, and junk. And now you can recycle stuff to get the advanced resources like chemicals, parts, and electronics. They are used both for crafting and building upgrades to the next tiers. And you can use it to trade later on - though, I'm not sure there will be an adequate trading system in the next update, but I'm going to implement it in a basic state at least.

The production system is also going through some changes. New items, new buildings, more usable items, upgrade items (like generators or tools). I think it would be expanded after the next update because there are not that many items you can craft right now - this should be improved and your ideas and suggestions are welcome!

The AI - same here, major improvements. There are new character needs (thirst, fun, social) and different ways for your survivors to interact with the world and your camp. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35874280/d23973732bfd7f46b5419c9c9c77718be214d426.png[/img]

[b]Overall roadmap:[/b]
[list]
[*] [b]v.0.7 [/b]- buildings, production, trade system prototype, improved AI. ETA - Late December 2021 or January 2022.
[*] [b]v.0.8[/b] - AI, more production items, and improved trade system. ETA - March 2022
[/list]
I hope everything will go as planned and there will be no major troubles ahead.

Again, thank you for your support and feedback. I think we're getting close to the finished state (well, after the next update :)) and this is truly amazing. Stay tuned, share your ideas and screenshots, and have fun!

notes.title: DevBlog - September-October 2021
notes.content:
Hi there! Sorry for being a little bit quiet about Project Apocalypse during the last few months. We've released a huge project at my workplace and it took almost all available energy from me. But I'm getting better now and I want to share with you some updates about the game.

So, current state - 0.6.1, Sandbox mode, survival, yay. Almost the whole base gameplay is there. Now it's time to improve the weak points and fill the game with more content. At this moment, I'm finalizing the reworked resources, production, and buildings documentation. You can always check the actual project documentation at [url=https://projectapocalypse.myjetbrains.com/youtrack/articles/]Knowledge Base[/url].

The building's list is going as planned, with minor changes and additions. In general, there will be more production buildings (weapon workshop, laboratory, clothing workshop, recycling, and some more), trade-related buildings (tradepost, "car parking" for raids), and social buildings (library, graveyard, shop). Most of the buildings will be upgradeable, both through leveling up and adding stuff to the buildings to improve them in some way.

Resource management is also being reworked. There are going to be more basic resources (building materials, metal, cloth, junk), recycled resources (parts, electronic components, and chemicals), alcohol, food, and water. There are also going to be more production schemes and items you can produce - from Rations (as a better food option) to some hardware equipment to upgrade your buildings or trade. New resources should be available in the next update, along with some of the new buildings. I hope it'll make the overall gameplay a bit deeper and finally will be able to provide the whole crafting and production experience I was planning to do.

So, a bit slow, but I'm moving forward with Project Apocalypse and I hope you'll be able to enjoy the next big update before the New Year :-)

Stay tuned and don't forget to post your ideas and feedback!

notes.title: DevBlog: Post-Launch
notes.content:
Hi there! First of all, I'd like to say Thank you to everyone who bought Project Apocalypse! You're amazing!

I want to share my current plans with you. After analyzing the initial feedback and going through my backlog, I've got three main task categories I'm working on right now:

1) "What is going on and how does it work?". UX and UI. "What does every building do", "where can you find your crafted weapon" and stuff like that. It's not clear right now and a lot of information is hidden from the player. This should be improved.

2) Job system improvement. Recurrent jobs and better job assigning logic. Currently, your survivor may stand near the Explore job marker, but the job will be assigned to another survivor at the other end of the map. That's a bit frustrating :D

3) New features and bug fixes. I want to make a prototype of the trading system and expand current interactive events a little bit. And there are infinite things to fix and improve - Infected spawn logic, combat system, visibility control, correct day-night cycle, building upgrade overhaul, and more...

I hope to release the updates every 2-4 weeks. So, thank you and stay tuned ;-)

notes.title: DevBlog - January 2021
notes.content:
Hi there!

From now on, I'll try to publish monthly update logs. I think it'll be better this way and will keep you informed about the Project Apocalypse state, in case you don't follow the social network accounts.

So, I'm still preparing for the early access launch. During the holidays, the game finally became playable (a little bit) and I was able to play for an hour last week. That's a pretty solid game session. 

There are a lot of things to fix and improve. I've added 70+ tasks to my task tracker during this session. But overall it's okay. You can build your base, craft basic items and weapons, upgrade buildings, explore the map for resources and defend against the infected.

I've finished 85 (documented) tasks during this month and some unknown number of extra things. There were a lot of bugfixes with AI and Job system, UI reworks, and game design tweaks.

I've managed to freeze the new feature implementation and now I'm focusing on bugfixes and tweaks to make the whole experience a bit more playable and enjoyable. Sure, it's fun to play if you know all the secret hotkeys and logic, but I think it must be clearer to the regular player. What each building and button do, how to manage jobs etc.

Still, there is one major feature left - saving the game. I was planning to postpone it, but looking at the current game session length I think it's a must-have. So, this and bugfixes\tweaks are my plans for February. 

Stay tuned for the updates!

notes.title: DevBlog 007
notes.content:
Hi there! Another dev blog with weekly changes, yay! Implemented this week:

[list]
[*]Fog of war tweaks and optimization
[*]Resource production
[*]Cannibalism
[*]New building construction system
[*]Improved AI (combat and peaceful)
[/list]

It looks kinda small, but it's 100+ changes here and there :-)

Fog of war unexpectedly consumed two evenings to optimize. It was working "okay" but there were problems with a huge amount of actors. I've split everything to "static" and "dynamic" fog of war objects and when tried to decrease the number of mask texture refresh calls. There are still a lot of things I can do with Fog of war, but I don't think it's the right time. It works and (almost) don't lag. So, moving forward with tasks.

The second main thing this week - I've reworked the building construction system. Now it's completely free, with custom position and rotation (and more to come). Because that is the only way to give you the ability to create your version of the camp. Surely, this system creates a lot of new problems, mostly with navigation. But I think it's better to solve these problems than to cut this cool and fun feature from the game.

Finally, I've organized most of my plans and tasks in public spreadsheet, so you can check what's going on and what's planned next:
[url=https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1A24bDTkcpXFlhv46sS5Pa8SgoMTpTsasRJrXyBVCZT8]Features and Tasks[/url]

notes.title: DevBlog 006
notes.content:
Today survivors died from hunger while standing next to the farm, filled with fresh food. Farm can produce resources now. But survivors can't get items from buildings yet.

Hi there! This was quite a productive week. General changes and improvements:
- Basic interaction with building. Survivors can get inside, rest inside the buildings and even get to the shooting positions outside.
- Production system, generating items and resources from other items and resources.
- Basic sound implementation. Now there are attacks, selection, interaction, death, gathering and many more sound effects.
- Explorable objects, hidden by default. Survivors can now find something (currently it's resource points) while exploring the map.
- Improved fog of war with correct post-process material (A colleague at work helped me with it and it is amazing)
- AI Director to control the infected and spawn the attack waves when needed.
- Context menu for interaction with ~most of the stuff
- Map size increased
- Infinite fixes and tweaks in the AI
- Testing, debugging, refactoring.

I always hope to finally record a gameplay video (that's like the last thing stopping me from early access preparation), but it never looks even remotely close to the game. AI Director helps, but the "camp" feeling is completely absent right now, with only 3 building types and disabled construction. But I'm pretty close to something playable, I think.

This week was okay. Could be better, but overall I'm quite happy with the results. I've had an optimistic plan to finish all things for the alpha version today and finally record a gameplay video, but still need more time. I think I'm pretty close, though.

I've been working on components and gameplay system this week. Two main tasks - Interaction with building (enter, exit, get to shooting point, rest etc) and Production. Both systems started to work today, but they are still unpolished and very raw.

I've also cleaning up and reworking project's documentation. I hope to get some help after launching the alpha version (it's better be called Early Pre-Alpha 0.0.1 :D), so it'll be nice to have proper feature list, roadmap, concept and stuff in one place instead of notes, papers, drawings and at least three separate services.

notes.title: DevBlog 004
notes.content:
Hi there!

This week, I tried to solve the "simple task" - make basic Fog of War system. As a gamer who grew up on Age of Empires and Warcraft, I thought it must be quite a trivial task, everyone can make it. Well... no. I managed to create a working prototype by the end of the week and I can use it to test the overall "do I need a fog of war" question. 

But it was a bit hard to find an adequate tutorials and solution. Most of them were like "now we'll write a 2000 lines of code algorythm" or "everything is done. Now just use your postprocess material which you don't have and don't have any idea how to make one" :D

[previewyoutube=hzaxBV4sd7s;full][/previewyoutube]

Current FoW implementation is very basic, but maybe it'll add enough to overall danger level of the game. And there is always room for improvement.

I've started to implement the context menu for player's actions. Now you can right click on ~anything and get the available options. It looks way cleaner that the old half-screen UI. I'm not sure if I'll be able to put the building logic in it, though. But I'll try.

I always playtest with x20 speed and that actually is a problem. Sure, you can find logic bugs faster, but it's not an actual gameplay. And when I tried to play on the standart speed - it was way to slow to be even remotely fun. I tweaked the delays between AI actions and removed x20 speed completely. Now I'm playing as a normal user and can improve the ACTUAL gameplay :D

Last, but not least - I've made my first build and uploaded it to Steam. Launched the game through Steam, made some screenshots. Quite a nice feeling, playing your own game in steam.

So, as always, stay tuned for more updates! ;-)

notes.title: DevBlog 003
notes.content:
Hi there!

Everything is fine. I had to take a break from Project Apocalypse and finish some IRL stuff. And so I failed all the planned features, roadmap, Early Access in december etc. But now everything is stable enough and I'm pushing the project forward. Yay! :D

For the last few weeks, I've been moving core gameplay stuff to C++ from Blueprints and working on the game systems and their interaction with each other. Hundreds of changes and almost every part of the project were affected... but it looks just like the november version and it's a little bit sad. I hope to finish the gameplay stuff soon and finally make an actual gameplay video.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35874280/7ec6d98a8f3154db6b7d10124bcfd3fc67637798.jpg[/img]

I've also removed the concrete dates from my roadmap. The main milestones are the same, but now I'll just be working on them and releasing updates when they're done. I still hope to launch Early Access soon, just after the basic game loop is not THAT bad :D

Today I was killing the survivors, by the way:
[list]
[*] First, they started to die from Hunger. 
[*] They learned how to use the Storage and get the food from it. And so they died after there was no food left.
[*] I fixed the hunger balance and they started to die from Exhaustion. For some reason, they couldn't find their Home and rest there.
[*] I've added a "rest without home" behavior and they still died, sometimes from hunger and sometimes from the lack of sleep.
[*] After the "priority need" function implementation, they started to die from hunger, with full inventory of food.
[*] I fixed the inventory logic and got an unplanned behavior...
[/list]

Now the survivors just sit on the food spawn point. They eat infinite food from "the bush" and then just sleep there, in the junk. And that's just their complete life cycle, all the basic needs are covered and they actually can just eat and sleep for the rest of their lives. That's creepy, a bit.

I need to fix inventory size, transportation, food generation (and maybe cooking for it?) and infinite amount of other things. But I'm glad that I'm moving with my project. Stay tuned ;-)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35874280/25da7227e571c210c4d6e032be3b7acff43f3855.png[/img]
